title: LEGO Explainer architecture
metaphor: Stack: runtimes at the bottom, the Python engine and the 3D viewer on top of them, the skill that drives both at the summit.

groups.title: Runtimes
groups.description: What everything runs on: Python for building, three.js in the browser for rendering.

groups.title: Engine
groups.description: Python package. Validates a build spec, injects it into the viewer, updates the gallery.

groups.title: Viewer
groups.description: Fixed three.js page. Draws the bricks, animates the explode, shows labels and popups.

groups.title: Skill
groups.description: The Claude instructions. Turns a target into a spec, then calls the engine.

pieces.title: Python 3.12
pieces.description: Stdlib only. Runs the validator and builder. No third-party packages.
pieces.details: The build side runs on plain Python 3.12 with only the standard library: json, argparse, pathlib, html. Nothing to pip install, so the engine works on any Mac with Homebrew Python and never breaks on a dependency upgrade.
pieces.example: python3 -m lego_explainer.build spec.json runs with a fresh interpreter and no virtualenv.

pieces.title: three.js
pieces.description: WebGL library. Renders meshes, lights, shadows. OrbitControls gives mouse orbit, zoom, pan.
pieces.details: three.js draws the model in the browser with WebGL. It supplies meshes, materials, lights and soft shadows. Its OrbitControls add turning the model with the mouse, zooming with the wheel and panning with a right-drag. The viewer uses version 0.160 through an import map.
pieces.example: Dragging left spins the camera around the model; the model itself never moves.

pieces.title: jsDelivr CDN
pieces.description: Serves three.js at load time. Offline means no model.
pieces.details: three.js is not bundled into the page. The browser fetches it from cdn.jsdelivr.net when the page opens. That keeps each build small, but the first open needs internet. If the download fails, the page shows a clear error after 6 seconds instead of a blank screen.
pieces.example: Opening a build on a plane with Wi-Fi off shows the 'could not start' message.

pieces.title: schema.py
pieces.description: Palette, shape heights, complexity-to-size table. The shared vocabulary.
pieces.details: One small module holds the rules every other part agrees on: the 12 LEGO colours, the height of each shape in plates, and the table that ties complexity to brick size. Change a rule here and both the validator and the docs follow.
pieces.example: Complexity 3 allows a footprint of 6 to 8 studs, so a 2x4 brick fits and a 2x2 does not.

pieces.title: build.py
pieces.description: CLI. Validates, writes the HTML and JSON into builds/, refreshes the gallery.
pieces.details: The command-line entry point. It reads the spec file, rejects NaN and malformed JSON, runs the validator, and on success writes <date>-<slug>.html and a copy of the spec into builds/, then refreshes the gallery. Errors are printed as a list and the exit code is 1.
pieces.example: Building the same spec twice on one day overwrites the page instead of making a duplicate.

pieces.title: validate.py
pieces.description: Rejects bad specs: unknown refs, overlaps, floating bricks, size not matching complexity. Reports every error at once.
pieces.details: Checks the whole spec in one pass and returns every problem it finds, so Claude can fix everything in one go. It checks field types, unknown fields, references to groups and colours, the complexity-to-size rule, bricks that overlap, and bricks with no studs underneath.
pieces.example: A brick placed on a tile comes back as 'floating', because tiles have no studs.

pieces.title: gallery.py
pieces.description: Writes builds/index.html. One card per build, newest first.
pieces.details: Rebuilds builds/index.html after every build. It reads each saved spec and shows one card per build with title, date, mode and piece count, newest first. Opening a card opens that build's page.
pieces.example: just run serves the gallery at localhost:5733.

pieces.title: Scene
pieces.description: Baseplate, lights, bricks with studs. Converts stud coordinates to 3D.
pieces.details: Turns the spec into 3D objects. One stud is one unit and a plate is 0.4 units tall. Each piece becomes a rounded box or an extruded slope with studs on top, placed on a grey baseplate that is sized to fit the model, under one sun light with shadows.
pieces.example: A 2x4 brick at level 3 becomes a box 2 by 1.2 by 4 units, sitting 1.2 units up.

pieces.title: Explode
pieces.description: Three states: assembled, groups apart, one group apart. Tweened in 0.6 s.
pieces.details: A small state machine with three states: assembled, groups pulled apart, and one group taken apart. Moving between states animates every brick for 0.6 seconds. Groups move away in proportion to where they sit, then any groups that still collide are pushed apart.
pieces.example: Press E to pull the groups apart, click the Engine group, press Esc to go back.

pieces.title: Hover label
pieces.description: Raycasts the pointer. Draws a leader line from brick to title.
pieces.details: Each frame, a ray is cast from the mouse into the scene to find the brick under the pointer. That brick gets a white outline, and a line runs from its top to a title label placed on the side away from the model's centre.
pieces.example: Hovering a brick on the right side of the model puts its label further to the right.

pieces.title: Popup
pieces.description: Click card: title, complexity dots, group, description.
pieces.details: Clicking a brick opens a card next to it. It shows the title, complexity as dots, the group, the short description in bold, a longer explanation, and an optional example. Clicking empty space or pressing Esc closes it.

pieces.title: SKILL.md
pieces.description: Workflow: understand target, decompose, pick mode, lay out bricks, build, report.
pieces.details: The instructions Claude follows. First it understands the target, then breaks it into groups and pieces, scores each piece's complexity, and picks themed or stack. It then places bricks on the stud grid, writes the text, runs the builder, and fixes any errors in at most three tries.
pieces.example: /lego-explainer ~/Documents/Scripts/home_guard ends with a new page in the gallery.

pieces.title: Samples
pieces.description: Two example specs. Test fixtures and layout patterns for Claude.
pieces.details: Two hand-made specs that pass validation: this stack model and a themed train. The tests use them to confirm the rules, and Claude reads them as layout references before placing bricks.
pieces.example: samples/themed.json shows how to lay a train along the z axis.
